shadow:
Underneath everything sits a single question. Why. It does not announce itself. It hums below the talking and the working and the falling asleep, and the mind treats it as a job to finish. So it builds. It reads, it argues, it picks a creed and sets it over the question like a lid. The lid holds for a while.

This is the harder thing to say. The world the mind shows you is not the world. It is a sketch, drawn fast, mostly right, and you live inside it and call it solid ground. Most people read this as sanity. It is closer to a kind of sleep with the eyes open. Everyone is doing it, which is why nobody names it.

The pressure is real, and the answer the mind reaches for never lands, because no sentence was going to close a thing this size. But the pressure is not the problem to solve. It is the door, mistaken for a wall. You do not get out by finding the right answer. You get out by noticing the question is alive, and turning to face it instead of patching over it, which feels like the wrong direction right up until it doesn't.
repressive: Some people give the question up. They go quiet, take the safe road through school or church or career, and decide the restlessness is just how they are. The mind looks settled. Under it, something never stopped asking.
reactive: Others seize one answer and clamp down hard. They find a leader, a system, a single truth, and they carry it outward and press it on people. The certainty runs loud. Beneath it sits an anger that keeps the real question out of earshot.
gift:
Put the book down and pick up a tool. A knife and a piece of green wood. A guitar. A trowel in cold ground. The hands start, and the mind, with nothing left to defend, begins to empty.

That emptying is inspiration. The word means filled with breath. Not a mood, not a good idea arriving. It is breath moving through you and out into something made, and each time it moves it dismantles a little of the sketch you had been calling reality. The made thing matters less than what the making does to the maker.

It comes when it comes. You cannot force it, and between the times it visits there are flat stretches that feel like nothing. The work asks for patience. But keep returning to the making and a floor builds under you, and the inspiration starts to carry its own warmth. A man whose wife had died poured a year of grief into a garden. Paths, ponds, dragonflies. At the end there was the garden, and a clear heart, and you could not say which one he had been building. The wound and the work were the same motion.
siddhi:
The asking simply stops. Not answered. Stopped. The pressure that used to grind in the head as why finds another road, out through the body and into everything, and a wide silence settles where the noise had been.

This is sanctity. The old word for it is kenosis, the emptying out, room made so something larger can come in. You are completely empty and somehow completely full, and there is no longer one who stands apart asking what it means. Life without answers. Just the mystery of who you are, worn close.

A person living here can look like a god to the rest of us, and we want to kneel, the one move that keeps us asleep. They are not above you. They are a mirror, holding up your own unremembered divinity. From here the whole road reads differently. The psychosis at the start, the lid, the long ache of the question, was not a sickness to be cured. It was the pressure, knocking to be let in.
